newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ming Pao to make large loan provision.
newsitem.headline: Ming Pao to make large loan provision.

text.p: Publisher Ming Pao Enterprise Corporation Ltd said it will need to make provisions in its 1996 accounts for the non-recovery of a loan.

Provisions for the non-recovery of a loan of HK$185.79 million will be reflected in the interim results of the company for the six-month period ended September 30, it said in a statement published on Tuesday.
The company said the non-payment of the loan would not have a material impact on its financial position and that the company would have sufficient working capital.

Ming Pao also said it is taking legal action against CIM Company Ltd to recover the HK$185.79 million loan and the unpaid accrued interest on the loan as well as a third party loan of HK$1.89 million and interest due on that loan.
The interest due was to have been calculated from April 1 at the Hong Kong prime lending rate plus one percent.

CIM is Ming Pao's former controlling shareholder and had agreed last October to indemnify Ming Pao again non-recovery of the principal if the loans were not recovered on or before March 31, 1996. CIM had agreed to give additional securities to Ming Pao and to repay the outstanding loans by September 30, but has not done so, said the Ming Pao statement.
